name: ThinkRail
description: ThinkRail for PI-Desktop: a spec-graph the agent can read, query and maintain (7 spec_* tools), 10 workflow skills (including the authoring checklist for the family), and a panel with a specs browser.
changelog: 1.4.0: the workflow family is resynced to upstream — #485 (entry scoping), #486 (PR template), #487 + #519 (PR completion modes), #520 (no per-round question cap), #517 (a message sent while the ask card is open queues instead of answering) — the port had been frozen at #485's parent commit. Entry is now scoped: onboarding, PR lifecycle, and changes that still have a product or design decision to make; a fully specified fix, a mechanical refactor, documentation, configuration-only work or a question proceeds directly and announces no routing. brainstorming asks for one review rather than a second approval round, reads `writing-specs` at the promote step, and names its Ending; choosing-a-workflow classifies on whether the work requires a product or design choice; spec-graph's blanket 'specs before code' becomes a proportional lookup; the three handoffs stop promising that all later work routes to brainstorming. shipping-a-pr gains the wait/snapshot completion modes, the body phase, the target repository's pull-request template, and the explicit merge-state set. asking-user-questions drops the per-round question cap, states that a composer message sent while the card is open queues behind it, and now describes this host's card truthfully (plain option labels, answers returned as a `question：answer` tool result). The always-on rule keeps upstream's three sentences; of its two former local differences the question carve-out is retired (upstream #485 settled the drift it compensated for) and the spec-graph precondition stays. Upstream carries its second standing rule (spec-graph's SPEC_RULE) in a second extension; this plugin keeps one, with that half living in the spec-graph skill's description and body. 1.3.0: the plugin is now exactly the workflow side — 7 spec_* tools, 10 skills, and a specs panel. Plugin file access no longer resolves a project of its own: the host roots every call by the invoking session, so the tools work even while the window shows no project, and the old cross-project warning is gone. A real failure now surfaces the host's own error unchanged. 1.2.0: the workflow family gets its standing entry back, through the host's own extension point. Upstream ThinkRail points the agent at its root router with an always-on rule (`before_agent_start`); PI-Desktop gives a plugin no prompt section, but it does give it `agent.extension` — so this plugin now declares that permission plus one dependency-free module (`extensions/workflow-rule.mjs`, 13 lines of code, no imports, no fs, no network) whose only job is to append that rule to the system prompt every turn. It lands after the skills catalog, AGENTS.md and project memory, which makes it the strongest instruction position the app offers. Two deliberate differences from upstream's rule: a pure question is stated as needing no routing (upstream leaves questions out of its trigger list while its router description claims them — a drift its own spec records), and the spec-graph case is stated as something to establish before classifying (an existing codebase with none is the onboarding case, handed to the user), rather than as a forced route — the router's own red flags say a forced route is worse than none. Trade-off, disclosed in safetyNotes: the module runs inside the agent process with the agent's tool permissions, so the plugin's fs-gateway sandbox no longer covers it — which is why the module is tiny and auditable. 1.1.0: the workflow family's authoring layer is ported — `writing-workflow-skills` (10 skills now). Upstream keeps the checklist in a skill and the rationale in a package spec; this host reads exactly one file per skill, so both layers are folded into that one file. 1.0.0: first PI-Desktop release — ported from dsh-plugin-thinkrail 1.0.0 (itself a port of JetBrains ThinkRail). 9 skills, and a specs view that docks in the right work panel.

en.name: ThinkRail
en.description: ThinkRail for PI-Desktop: a spec-graph the agent can read, query and maintain (7 spec_* tools), 10 workflow skills (including the authoring checklist for the family), and a panel with a specs browser.
en.safetyNotes: Reads and writes project files through the host fs gateway (declared scope: read anywhere in the project, write only .md files and the .thinkrail/ scratch dir, delete only files it wrote, always to the system trash); the host resolves every path against the project of the session that invoked the tool, so the plugin never picks a project itself. Ships ONE agent-process extension (`extensions/workflow-rule.mjs`, declared under contributes.agentExtensions, requires agent.extension): 13 lines of code (62 with its rationale comment), no imports, no filesystem access, no network — it only appends a fixed paragraph to the system prompt each turn, pointing the agent at the choosing-a-workflow skill. That module runs inside the agent process with the agent's own tool permissions, so it is NOT covered by the fs gateway above; read it before enabling. Registers 7 agent tools and 10 skills (skills are prose; no code runs from them); sends nothing over the network and reads no credentials.

zh-CN.name: ThinkRail
zh-CN.description: PI-Desktop 版 ThinkRail：agent 可读、可查、可维护的 spec 图（7 个 spec_* 工具）、10 篇工作流技能（含编写工作流技能的清单与元规则），以及一个含 spec 浏览器的面板。
zh-CN.safetyNotes: 文件的读写一律走宿主的 fs 网关（已声明的范围：项目内可读，只写 .md 与 .thinkrail/ 草稿目录，只删本插件写过的文件，且删到系统回收站）；宿主按发起调用的会话解析每一个路径，插件自己不判定项目。**附带一个 agent 进程内扩展**（`extensions/workflow-rule.mjs`，声明在 contributes.agentExtensions，需要 agent.extension 权限）：13 行代码（含注释共 62 行）、无任何 import、不碰文件系统、不发起网络请求——只把一段固定文字追加到每轮系统提示末尾，指向 choosing-a-workflow 技能。该模块运行在 agent 进程内、权限等同于 agent 自身工具，**不受上面那条 fs 网关约束**；启用前请阅读该文件。注册 7 个模型工具与 10 篇技能（技能全是文字说明，不执行任何代码）；不发起任何网络请求，也不读取凭据。

author: andrewliu

agentTools.name: spec_grep
agentTools.description: search the project's spec-graph by content (narrowable by metadata); reach for it before grep/read when exploring or planning. Matches within spec files only (files whose frontmatter carries `id` + `type`), optionally narrowed by type / tag / parent / depends-on. Returns path:line matches with a snippet; read a matched file's body with the normal read tool.

agentTools.name: spec_get
agentTools.description: look up one spec by id: its frontmatter, resolved links, and path (read the body with `read`). Resolves forward and reverse edges across parent / depends-on / references / implements. Returns no prose body.

agentTools.name: spec_graph
agentTools.description: walk a bounded slice of the spec-graph (subtree / ancestors / neighbors) from a node. `subtree` goes down the parent tree, `ancestors` up to the tree root, `neighbors` across a chosen edge and its reverse. Bounded by `depth` (default 1).

agentTools.name: spec_create
agentTools.description: create a new spec file with scaffolded frontmatter (id/type/title/links) and heading stubs. Fails if the file already exists, the id is already in use, or the path is not an indexable root-relative .md path. Edit prose afterward with the write/edit tools.

agentTools.name: spec_update
agentTools.description: edit a spec's frontmatter only (scalar fields + list entries); never its prose. Preserves the file's field order, comments, and non-dialect fields. Prose is edited with the write/edit tools.

agentTools.name: spec_delete
agentTools.description: delete a spec file by id, to the system trash. Other specs may still reference it afterward — run spec_validate to find dangling links.

agentTools.name: spec_validate
agentTools.description: check the spec-graph for dangling links, duplicate ids, and parent cycles.
